A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SeaLion paper and Appendices A–C. All 20 pages were compared; pages 2–20 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance. The first-page changes are fully readable.

before.justification: v1 reports original ShapeNet and IntrA generation experiments, semi-supervised training, segmentation augmentation, and supplementary analyses in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original empirical results, including the generation and downstream segmentation experiments in Section 4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The architecture, training objectives, joint noise/segmentation prediction, inference procedure, and editing algorithm are identical in Section 3 and the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six ShapeNet categories and IntrA data, with unchanged generation, semi-supervised learning, segmentation augmentation, and part-aware editing tasks.

E2.justification: DiffFacto and the Lion-based comparisons, including Lion & PointNet++ and Lion & SPoTr, retain the same participation in the corresponding main-text and appendix experiments.

E3.justification: Data splits, training budgets, metrics, and experimental procedures are unchanged. This includes the 8k/24k training stages and the semi-supervised study's 10% labeled/90% unlabeled split.

E4.justification: The diffusion-step analysis, segmentation-branch study, semi-supervised analysis, and qualitative failure examples are identical, including Figure 5, Table 7, and Appendix C.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical throughout the text, tables, and figures. No repeated-run, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information is added or removed.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports IntrA 1-NNA (p-CD) values of 65.22% for SeaLion and 71.74% for DiffFacto in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and reasoning are identical, including the training objectives, p-CD definition in Equations 11 and 16, and metric arguments in Appendix A.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions, performance claims, and application claims. The added code-access statement does not revise their scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of inter-part coherence, metric limitations, and segmentation/noise feature alignment remain identical. No substantive explanation, limitation, or applicability qualification changes.

D1.justification: v2 adds a 'Code available at' statement and a direct SeaLion GitHub repository link to the abstract; v1 lacks this pointer. Implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and training-time disclosures are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning, and all 42 references are unchanged. The new repository link does not add a cited research work.

P1.justification: The only prose addition is the code-availability statement in the abstract; the arXiv version/date stamp also changes. Section order and all other wording remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added repository line slightly reflows the abstract and opening introduction on page 1. Figures and tables are unchanged, and pages 2–20 render identically.

improvement.justification: The new repository pointer modestly improves implementation discoverability and reproducibility information. Scientific content and supporting evidence, including the appendices, remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the added access information but cannot verify repository availability or code quality.
